newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST-POLISH 52-WK,13-WK T-BILL YIELD SEEN DOWN.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-POLISH 52-WK,13-WK T-BILL YIELD SEEN DOWN.

text.p: Banks expect the average yield on Poland's benchmark 52-week T-bill to fall to 18.08 percent at the end of 1997 against 21.11 percent at the last primary sale, a Reuters poll of the country's 26 largest banks showed.
Last month, banks saw the benchmark yield falling to 17.76 percent by year-end.
The end-1997 forecasts ranged from 17.00 to 20.20 percent.
Banks expected the 52-week average yield to ease to 17.73 percent in March 1998 with a range of forecasts of 15.75 to 19.70 percent.
They expected the yield to rise to 21.19 percent on average at the end of the month with a forecast range from 20.60 to 21.70 percent.
The average yield on the 13-week T-bill was also seen falling to 17.74 percent by year-end from 20.82 percent at the last primary auction, the poll showed.
Last month banks expected a yield fall to 17.34 percent.
The 13-week T-bill yield forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 16.50 percent to 19.25 percent.
The yield was seen falling to 17.34 percent in March 1998 with a forecast range between 15.50 and 18.80 percent.
Banks expected it to rise to 20.88 percent this month with a range from 20.20 to 21.60 percent.
